summary: This note is a Wikipedia-style biographical introduction to Sir Edwin Landseer Lutyens (1869–1944), an English architect known for adapting traditional architectural styles to the needs of his era. It states that he designed many English country houses, war memorials and public buildings. It also quotes two critics: Christopher Hussey, who wrote that Lutyens was widely held to be the greatest architect since Wren, and Gavin Stamp, who called him the greatest British architect of the twentieth century or of any other.
one_line: Biographical note on Sir Edwin Lutyens, English architect (1869–1944) known for country houses, war memorials and public buildings, praised by critics.
key_facts: Sir Edwin Landseer Lutyens was born on 29 March 1869 and died on 1 January 1944.
Edwin Lutyens was an English architect.
Edwin Lutyens was known for imaginatively adapting traditional architectural styles to the requirements of his era.
Edwin Lutyens designed many English country houses.
Edwin Lutyens designed many war memorials.
Edwin Lutyens designed many public buildings.
In his biography, the writer Christopher Hussey wrote that Edwin Lutyens was widely held in his lifetime to be the greatest architect since Wren.
Christopher Hussey wrote that Edwin Lutyens was widely held to be 'our greatest architect since Wren if not, as many maintained, his superior'.
The architectural historian Gavin Stamp described Edwin Lutyens as 'surely the greatest British architect of the twentieth (or of any other) century'.
